pr.title: Say only what this machine knows in the DRAFT event
pr.head: eca70d6b82e705a27e60ab92b9f52148eb157576

summary: Projector's watch daemon is one process per machine that polls the pull requests its agent sessions subscribe to, and sends each session event lines that say what to do. A session that pushed to a pull request holds its fix role, and hears DRAFT when the pull request is a draft that no review has signed off and no session on this machine reviews. Before this change, the line told the agent to "tell the user that no session reviews" the pull request. The daemon cannot see sessions on other machines, so a person who reviews from a second machine kept hearing that their pull request would go unreviewed (#411).
This change fixes that in three ways:

1. The wording says only what this machine knows. The line now tells the agent to say that no session on this machine reviews the pull request, and fix-pr tells it never to say that no session reviews it at all.
  2. A review running elsewhere holds the event back. A review posts a start comment on the pull request when it begins and deletes it when it publishes. While such a comment for the current head is live, the daemon announces no DRAFT. The daemon already read those comments in in_flight, so the reading moves into a shared live_starts generator.
  3. Only a trusted account's start comment counts, and a head is still announced once. In a public repository anyone can comment, so only a start comment from an account whose review would count holds the event back. While the event is held back, the head keeps its key in the session's state, so a review that ends without signing the head off does not announce it a second time.

The first review, of ae778fa, found that a review elsewhere made the daemon announce DRAFT twice for one head. eca70d6 fixes that and takes both suggestions from that review. The review of eca70d6 is clean.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Start comment: the comment project review setup posts when a review begins, carrying a projector-start marker with the head SHA and the model. publish deletes it.
  • Live: a start comment that review.is_live says still means a review in progress. It stops being live once its model publishes a verdict on that head, or a day after it was last edited.
  • standing: the helper in route_fix that announces a key once and records it in the session's state, so the next pass does not repeat it.
  • Counted account: one whose review review.review_counts accepts. In a public repository that is an OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR. In a private or internal repository it is every account.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Review of ae778fa: changes requested. One finding: the daemon announced DRAFT twice for one head after a review elsewhere. Two suggestions: update the watch-daemon plan, and count only trusted accounts' start comments.
  • eca70d6 fixes the finding and takes both suggestions. Its review is clean, with one suggestion: also count the operator's own start comment.
  • Open question to the user: should a Projector verdict on the head also hold DRAFT back? Today it does not.

groups.title: The daemon holds DRAFT back while a review runs anywhere
groups.kicker: The event's condition and wording, and the shared start-comment reader
intro: route_fix decides what a session with the fix role hears on each pass. Its DRAFT branch now holds the event back while a live start comment for the head comes from a counted account, and its line says "no session on this machine reviews". While the event is held back, the branch keeps the head's key from the last pass, as the CONFLICT branch does while GitHub has not computed mergeability. The GraphQL query now asks for each comment's authorAssociation, the field the check reads.

live_starts yields every live start comment for the head, from any account and model. in_flight, which keeps the review role from re-announcing a head a review is already working on, now filters that output to its own reviewer and model, and skips the start comment this machine's review state records. Its behavior does not change.

files.note: The DRAFT condition, key, and wording in route_fix, the comment field in the query, and live_starts split out of in_flight.

checks.text: With the test harness's fake gh: in a public repository, a live start comment from OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR holds DRAFT back, and one from CONTRIBUTOR, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR, or NONE does not. In a private repository, any account's comment holds it back.

Over four passes (no start comment, a live one, the review publishing changes-requested, a quiet pass), the daemon announces DRAFT once for the head, and the key stays in the state while the event is held back. The previous head announced it twice.

The check reads only the association. review.counted_reviews also counts the reviewer's own reviews by login, so in a public repository where the operator is only a CONTRIBUTOR, the operator's own review on another machine does not hold the event back. The review lists this as a suggestion.
in_flight keeps the same filter as before: the reviewer's login, the model, and not the recorded start comment. The existing in_flight tests pass at this head.

groups.title: The fixer's instructions, the event table, and the plan
groups.kicker: What fix-pr tells the agent to say, the docs row for DRAFT, and the watch-daemon plan
intro: fix-pr is the skill a fixing session runs, and its event notes say how to answer each event. The DRAFT note now explains that the daemon sees only this machine, and tells the agent to say that no session on this machine reviews the pull request, unless the user reviews it elsewhere. The event table in docs/cli.md names the start-comment condition, and the watch-daemon plan records the rule.

files.note: The DRAFT note: the new wording, and that a live start comment elsewhere also silences the event.
The DRAFT row of the event table names the start-comment condition.
§ 2.7's DRAFT row gains the start-comment condition and the new wording. The § 9.1 bullet on announcing only work gains the rule at its end. No section is renumbered.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Tests for the new condition and the single announcement
intro: test_a_draft_another_machine_is_reviewing_asks_the_fixer_for_nothing gives three drafts a live start comment each: one for the current head, one for an older head, and one from an account whose review would not count. It expects DRAFT for the second and third only. test_a_review_elsewhere_does_not_announce_a_draft_head_twice runs a review on another machine through to a changes-requested verdict and expects one DRAFT. The test of every event kind expects the new wording.

checks.text: Against the previous head's watch.py, both start-comment tests fail. At this head all 107 watch tests pass.
